extracted.intended_audience: general public and journalists interested in media accountability
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for responsible investigative and feature reporting, emphasizing verification, editorial oversight, transparency with readers, and consideration of societal impacts when reporting on sensitive allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification in multiple directions
rubrics_metrics.description: "What you’re supposed to do is verify in multiple directions, in multiple ways, from as many sources and resources as you can think of what occurred and why."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts through multiple independent directions and methods; corroborate key elements of the story rather than relying solely on a single source or the subject's account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency with readers about what is known and how
rubrics_metrics.description: "And to be clear with readers what you know, what you don’t know and how you know those things."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly disclose to readers the limits of reporting, the degree of confirmation for claims, and the methods/sources used so audiences can judge reliability; transparency helps maintain reader trust and may prevent poor editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting people who could verify or dispute key elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The report criticized that the writer and editorial colleagues "decided not to contact people who could have verified or disputed key elements of the victim’s tale."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek out and contact witnesses, named parties, organizations, and other potential corroborators or disputers of important claims before publishing; omission of such contacts is a serious lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous editorial and fact-checking process and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure was described as "top to bottom, of Rolling Stone’s editorial process from the reporter to her lead editor to the fact-checker to the overall managing editor, Will Dana."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear, functioning roles for reporters, editors, and fact-checkers; enforce standards consistently and hold individuals accountable when systemic failures occur (including managerial responsibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present unverified allegations as cinematic narrative or facts
rubrics_metrics.description: "What you can’t do is assert these things and present it as a narrative in a cinematic fashion and seemingly present that as almost fact."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dramatizing or narrativizing unconfirmed allegations; clearly label conjecture or unverified narrative elements and resist storytelling techniques that imply unproven events happened as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize specifically and comprehensively when errors harm identifiable parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporter's apology "went to her editors and colleagues, went to her readers, went to the University of Virginia, but notably didn’t single out the fraternity itself," described as "a very stingy, parsimonious apology."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing errors causes reputational or other harm, apologies should specifically acknowledge affected parties and the nature of the mistake rather than issuing vague or incomplete statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider broader societal impact when reporting on sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that the article "will affect the credibility of other rape and sexual assault cases" and that reporting choices can influence how victims and accusers are treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the potential effects of reporting on public perception, future victims, and institutional responses—especially for sensitive subjects like sexual assault—and exercise extra care to avoid undermining legitimate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document editorial choices to enable re-evaluation during reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: "The very act of writing on a screen or on a piece of paper a choice that you made that doesn’t bear up to scrutiny might tell you to say, ‘you know what, I’m going to stop right there. We’re going to go back and revisit this.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep written records of sourcing decisions and editorial judgments during reporting so choices can be reviewed and reversed if later scrutiny shows they are unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate legal and reputational risks of publishing serious allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of Virginia chapter of the fraternity "announced today that it will pursue legal action against the magazine, calling the publishing of its retracted story reckless."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential legal exposure and reputational consequences before publishing allegations that could harm identifiable organizations or individuals; involve legal counsel or higher editorial review when necessary.
